description: Reads a reference picture the page should match (a photo, artwork, mockup or screenshot in the project, e.g. refs/01.jpg) at full resolution, in one call and with no page open: `crop` [left, top, right, bottom] in the picture's pixels, enlarged up to 4× to fit 1280 px, with `grid` lines every N px labelled in the picture's own pixel coordinates (positions read off it go straight into the next call or the scene), and `sample` points, each answered as #rrggbb. With the page open, `compare: true` puts the picture, the page's look (from `camera` when given) and a difference picture side by side and says what share of pixels differ, overall and in a grid of regions (`cells` per side, 4 by default), with each `sample` point's colour on both, or that the canvas aspect is not the picture's. Use it to read a picture the page should match and to check the page against it.

camera.description: For compare: the page's look from this position (looking at lookAt) or from a camera by name, as `look`'s camera; left out, the picture's entry in refs/cameras.json when there is one, else the page's own camera.

cells.description: Regions per side for compare's differing-share grid (4 by default).

compare.description: Put the open page's look beside the picture with their differences; needs `open` first, and a canvas with the picture's aspect for the pixel comparison.

crop.description: [left, top, right, bottom] in the picture's pixels ([x, y, width, height] is read as such when right < left or bottom < top), trimmed to the picture; the whole picture when left out. With compare: that region of the picture and the same region of the page, enlarged side by side with their differences.

file.description: The picture's path, relative to cwd, or the name of a baseline saved with look { save } (compare the page with its earlier look).

game.description: The name the game was opened under with the `open` tool, to act on ("main" by default; a subagent uses its own).

grid.description: Gridline spacing in the picture's pixels (100 on a whole picture, 10 to 50 on a crop); none when left out.

sample.description: Points [x, y] in the picture's pixels whose colour to return (the mean of 5 × 5 pixels); with compare, the page's colour at the same point too.

name: reference
